text:
kai: @channel CI apply for gpu-pool moved our TF backend from S3->GCS and one of the import steps failed mid-run, leaving a lock and partial state. pipeline: https://git.redwood/infra/pipelines/2387 — anyone oncall?
maria: on it. Which region and which pipeline job exactly?
kai: eu-west1, pipeline #2387 runner-5. error in job log: 'error importing resource: provider plugin mismatch' then apply aborted, lock still held.
terraform-bot: terraform-bot: Lock acquired by pipeline-2387 (runner-5) at 1768504319 for backend gcs://redwood-tfstate/eu/gpu-pool.tfstate
sam: I can access the GCS bucket and check the lock file. Give me a sec.
sam: found lock: {"ID":"pipeline-2387","Creator":"runner-5","Created":1768504319} — runner-5 pod is gone. looks like orphaned lock.
maria: ugh. runner died during import. two risks: 1) force-unlock could race with another CI apply, 2) import partial state means some resources exist in cloud but not in state.
olivia: cost note: this gpu-pool has a separate problem — we discovered eu-west1 has 3 extra p4d nodes from previous test overlay, raising monthly spend ~30%. splitting state per-region would let us rollout fixes region-by-region.
devops-bot: devops-bot: flagged incident RED-352 (tfstate-lock-orphan) and created runbook link: https://wiki.redwood/infra/tfstate-locks
maria: plan: 1) prevent CI applies to eu-west1 by flipping pipeline flag, 2) manual force-unlock once we've confirmed no active runners, 3) run `terraform state list` in a local workspace to identify missing imports, 4) perform targeted `terraform import` for the dangling resources, 5) apply and verify.
kai: do we have an easy way to detect provider version drift that caused the import fail? I saw provider changes in the PR that moved backend — provider bumped from google v4 -> v5.
sam: yes, I'll run `terraform providers lock` and compare lockfile on repo vs the workspace. Quick command I used:```bash
git checkout infra/tfstate-backend-change
terraform init -backend-config=backend.gcs.conf
cat .terraform.lock.hcl | grep google -A2
```
maria: also adding a pre-apply CI check to abort if a backend lock exists and to refuse concurrent runs for the same statefile. quick patch: adds `gsutil stat gs://.../tfstate-lock` check and `terraform force-unlock --check` step (dry-run).
olivia: for cost mitigation I opened a small PR to remove the 3 leftover p4d nodes and added an autoscale guard in the helm chart. linking PR: https://git.redwood/infra/pulls/4123
terraform-bot: terraform-bot: Lock manually force-unlocked by maria at 1768504445 (reason: orphaned runner).
maria: after unlock I ran `terraform state pull > state.json` and inspected `state.json` for resources in module.gpu that are not present. Found 2 orphaned `google_compute_instance` that needed import: `redwood-gpu-eu-01` and `redwood-gpu-spot-02`.
sam: performed `terraform import module.gpu.google_compute_instance.redwood-gpu-01 projects/redwood/zones/eu-west1-b/instances/redwood-gpu-01` and same for spot-02. import succeeded.
maria: then `terraform plan` showed no drifts, followed by `terraform apply` from a locked maintenance runner. apply completed, state consistent.
kai: great. Follow-ups: - add backend lock_ttl to 300s for GCS backend - add CI pre-check to block concurrent applies to same statefile - implement region-split migration proposal (doc in PR 4123)
olivia: I'll own the region-split RFC and cost cleanup. tagging infra-runbook to update the tfstate recovery steps. :thumbsup:
maria: closing thread — if anyone sees residual drift open a new thread and reference RED-352.
